key_insight: The paper shows that quantum PDE solvers must be benchmarked under a shared readout contract, because performance changes dramatically with discretization, sampling, and reconstruction choices.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum computing, the benchmark identifies which methods are actually usable for the 1-D heat equation on current simulators and hardware-like noise models, and when simpler observables are far cheaper to estimate than full fields.
method: Compared 11 quantum kernels on the same 1-D Dirichlet heat-equation instances.
Tested three initial conditions, four grid sizes (n=4 to 7 qubits), fixed final time T=1, and multiple backends: statevector, ideal-shot, and noisy Aer.
Included coherent linear solvers, variational and imaginary-time methods, Hamiltonian-simulation variants, and spectral quantum simulation.
evidence_signal: On statevector, QSM and Schade-Hamiltonian matched the semi-discrete reference to floating-point precision, Schrödingerisation reached about 1e-4 error, and fixed-shot runs pushed HHL to roughly 0.79 relative L2 error.
watch_item: Some reported errors are strongly affected by reconstruction normalization and postselection/readout costs, so implementation details can dominate apparent solver quality.
paper_title: Quantum PDE Solvers in Practice: Application-Driven Benchmarking of the Heat Equation
